exceptions.rationale: The current lockfile resolves picomatch 4.0.7 through Astro/Vite and a nested 2.3.2 through anymatch. GitHub's reviewed advisory currently lists no patched release. The published site is a static Astro build; repository inspection shows picomatch only as a transitive build-tool dependency, with no direct application import or request-time glob parsing. This reduces exposure but does not remediate the vulnerable code.
mitigations: Keep SmartPickHub as a static build with no Node.js request-time server or runtime glob processing.
Do not pass visitor-controlled values, catalogue content, or external inputs into glob patterns during builds.
Keep package-lock.json committed and use npm ci for reproducible installs.
Retain the full npm audit output in every CI artifact; do not suppress this advisory or label the audit clean.
Monitor the upstream picomatch advisory and release; PR #238 is an upstream proposal, not a merged or released fix.
Reassess immediately when an upstream patched version is published and no later than the expiry date.

lastNpmAuditObserved.note: A clean npm audit result does not prove installed picomatch copies are patched; the project lockfile was not remediated and the upstream advisory remains published.

exceptions.advisoryMetadataNote: The GitHub advisory page currently displays package/affected-version metadata as unknown and no patched version; do not interpret npm audit zero findings as proof of a patched package.
